steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Definition: Structure analysis examines how a text is organised - the order of ideas, paragraphing, sentence variety, and narrative techniques used to shape meaning. | Openings: How does the text begin? What effect does the opening have? - In media res (starting in the middle of the action) - Setting the scene - Creating mystery or intrigue | Endings: How does the text conclude? What is the final impression? - Resolution or closure - Cliffhanger or ambiguity - Reflective circular ending | Narrative Perspective: Who is telling the story? - First person (I, we) - personal, subjective - Third person (he, she, they) - more detached - Omniscient narrator - knows everything

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: What is the difference between language and structure analysis? | Why might a writer use a short paragraph? | What does "in media res" mean?

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Openings, Endings, Narrative Perspective, and one past-paper question.
